newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-STEWARDS THE KEY TO SECURITY AT 1998 WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STEWARDS THE KEY TO SECURITY AT 1998 WORLD CUP.

text.p: Stewards at stadiums will be the key to security during the 1998 soccer World Cup in France, the French government delegate to the tournament said on Thursday.

Stewards, who will be called "stadiers", a word created in a bid to avoid the invasion of English words into the French language known as franglais, will be used to "welcome, escort and lead spectators" inside stadiums.

The system has been widely used in Britain, especially during the European championship last year, but is new to France. Only two French stadiums, Paris' Parc des Princes and Marseille's Stade Velodrome already use stewards.
A 1995 bill made stadium owners responsible for security in the stands.
World Cup organisers said they would start recruiting about 5,000 stewards aged 18 to 30 for the finals, one third of whom would be professionals, two thirds of whom would be volunteers.
"It will allow the police to concentrate on other tasks," government World Cup delegate Noel de Saint-Pulgent said.
